title: Compacting ingest frontier with ID mapping and lossless reordering
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Our current log ingress handles high-cardinality structured JSON but suffers from two production issues: (1) correlation IDs get lost or rewritten when records are compacted and sharded across tenant routers, causing traces to disconnect in downstream tracing dashboards; (2) transient out-of-order delivery from edge relays causes downstream chunking to duplicate work and inflate storage/ingest cost. Goal: Build an ingest-frontier component that performs compacting/merging of structured events while preserving original correlation IDs via a deterministic ID-mapping layer, and guarantees lossless reordering semantics for events within a bounded time window. This component should integrate with the existing Loki/ELK sinks and emit stable metadata used by tracing hooks and the Console latency/error dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress front-end accepts existing JSON schema and annotates events with stable_correlation_id without mutating original fields
Compaction reduces redundant prefix tokens across a tenant stream by >=35% on tail-latency workloads
Reordering window (configurable, default 10s) guarantees exactly-once ordering semantics for events within window; downstream dedupe verifies no duplicates introduced
No more than 5% p99 ingest-latency regression compared to baseline when under normal load; falls back to pass-through if overloaded
End-to-end trace join tests show traced spans reconnect when stable_correlation_id is used by tracing hooks and dashboards
design_notes: Component sits in front of the existing shard router: edge -> ingest-frontier -> tenant-router -> chunker -> storage/sinks

ID mapping uses a tenant-scoped, monotonic fingerprint: hash(original_cid || tenant_id || event_timestamp_floor) to produce stable_correlation_id. Mapping table is ephemeral (TTL 24h) and sharded by consistent-hash to avoid cross-node lookups

Compaction algorithm: stream-aware rolling window that delta-encodes repeated keys and prefixes; configurable heuristics to avoid compaction for high-cardinality fields (user_id/email) to reduce decompression cost
Reordering: sequence-buffer with watermark advancement informed by clock-skew estimation; deliver in-order to downstream with de-duplication token (stable_correlation_id + sequence_index)
Failure mode: when ingress-frontier cannot persist mapping state, it falls back to passthrough with a metric and alert; lossless guarantees relaxed to best-effort until recovery
Trade-offs considered: strong consistency (centralized mapping) vs. availability. Chosen: eventually-consistent, sharded mapping with short TTL to balance latency and memory footprint

Privacy: original correlation IDs are not stored beyond TTL in plaintext in the mapping service; the stable_correlation_id is derived via HMAC with tenant-specific key stored in KMS to prevent cross-tenant correlation by Ops
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature branch + unit/integration tests; dry-run in canary cluster emitting stable_correlation_id header only
Phase 1: 5% traffic for low-risk tenants; enable compaction heuristics (non-default) and track metrics
Phase 2: 25% traffic; enable reordering buffer with short window (3s); run end-to-end trace join smoke tests
Phase 3: 100% gradual ramp; bake for 48h; enable full compaction and 10s reordering window; finalize defaults
Rollback: toggle to passthrough via runtime flag; plan automated rollback if error-rate or p95-ingest-latency breaches threshold
test_plan: Unit tests for mapping deterministic properties and TTL eviction
Integration tests with tenant-router + chunker to validate in-order delivery and dedupe under simulated network reorder
Load test: replay 24h customer workload in staging to measure compaction ratio and CPU/memory impact
Tracing integration test: synthetic trace generator verifies correlation stitching using stable_correlation_id across API/gateway/worker spans
Chaos test: kill mapping shard processes and verify passthrough fallback and automated recovery metrics
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: ingress-frontier throughput, compaction ratio, mapping-table size per shard, reordering-buffer occupancy
Alerts: mapping-table OOM risk > 80% capacity; compaction-induced CPU > 70% baseline; p50/p95 ingest latency regression > 10%
SLOs: ingestion availability 99.95% for pass-through; compaction-enabled SLO target 99.9% (degraded tolerated during rollouts)
Audit logs: emit mapping state changes and passthrough toggles to Console for postmortem analysis
